You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: every wrong submission costs 1 and every demo request costs 1. An
instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt cap is reached, and
reaching the cap is charged the full cap. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

# Continual-ARC

Treat each puzzle instance as a strict action protocol: the entire reply must be exactly one JSON object (`submit` with a grid, `request_demos`, or `finish`), with no preceding or trailing explanation, Markdown, or other text. Do not call shell or other tools to send an action; the JSON reply itself is the action.
2. Read attempt and demo budgets. Request demos only when their expected information is worth the cost; account for demo-request costs as well as wrong submissions. Before guessing, compare all supplied input-output pairs cell by cell, record the exact changed cells and unchanged candidate objects, and test a rule against every pair. Do not act on an analogy or a partial alignment until it explains every observed change and non-change. If the rule remains ambiguous and budget permits, request another demo.
3. Derive output dimensions and layout from the demonstrations. Apply the supported rule, preserve all other cells, then check row count, each row length, cell range (0–9), and JSON validity before submitting.
4. After feedback, revise the hypothesis only from the correctness result or a new demo. A correct/incorrect result does not identify which cells were wrong; do not treat speculative explanations as evidence. Submit only when the rule is sufficiently supported; use `finish` only after the instance is over.
